complexity_matrix.notes: One address computation, base + mid * sizeof(element). No pointer chase.
ceil(log2(N+1)) comparisons worst case; O(1) when the target sits at the first midpoint. Derivation: cost-derivations#halving.
Best case is logarithmic, not constant: absence is only concluded once the window empties, which takes at least log2(N+1) halvings.
One element comparison plus at most two integer comparisons to select a branch; window shrinks by at most half.
W(t+1) = ceil(W(t)/2), so the retained window is at most half the previous one. This is the whole source of the logarithmic bound.
First index at or after a value. Answers 'count of elements below x' and 'insert position' without a separate scan.
Halving still log N iterations, but each midpoint costs a walk from the head. Strictly worse than a linear scan — the power comes from O(1) random access.

complexity_matrix.operation: Batch of n queries over one sorted array
complexity_matrix.notes: Random targets average a constant number of probes; the n log N figure is the adversarial worst case.
Record the hit, then re-search [lo, mid) for the same value. Second logarithmic pass.
Two boundary descions bracket the run, then k steps walk it. The +k is unavoidable output cost.
Sort cost dominates when the queried fraction of elements exceeds roughly log N out of every N.

correctness_argument.claim: Each branch discards only indices provably unable to hold the target, so the window invariant is preserved and emptiness at exit proves absence rather than merely failing to observe it.

cost_derivations.claim: W(t+1) = ceil(W(t)/2) gives W(k) = ceil(N / 2^k); the loop ends at the smallest k with 2^k > N, i.e. exactly ceil(log2(N+1)) comparisons.

limits.claim: In the comparison decision-tree model a correct search needs N leaves in a tree of depth k with at most 2^k leaves, forcing k >= ceil(log2 N); binary search attains it, so no comparison-based search does better. No deterministic worst-case O(1) hash lookup is known in general.

supporting_structure.name: Monotone Sorted Sequence with O(1) Random Access
supporting_structure.rationale: The technique's entire advantage is the combination of sorted order with constant-time indexing. Sortedness supplies the discard rule (one comparison eliminates a half) and contiguous storage supplies the O(1) probe; remove either and the bound collapses to O(N log N) or to a prerequisite sort. This structure is not an auxiliary choice, it is the precondition the correctness argument depends on.
